why: Word heads gain over long streams on the test bed, 0.023 on its own cell shape and 0.017 on the full size's, all of it memory (word_rhythm.json, full_size_shape_bed.json). Knowledge cells also gained early, and with four times the data their lead shrank within the run from 0.022 to 0.011 (knowledge_data_scaling.json). Does the word heads' gain hold as the data grows, or fade as an early help does? It bears on the full-size run (full_size_word_heads.json), which trains on 3.75 times the bytes of the test bed's 24,000 updates (368.6M against 98.3M).

arms.fan2-24k: the test bed with the full size's cell shape (--granule-fan 512 --granule-cells 681), 24,000 updates, cosine over 24,000
arms.fan2-word-24k: the same with one word head a read (--read-word-heads 1 --read-word-span 32)

training: On streams (--stream 10 --stream-groups 3), seed 20001, on the laptop's GPU, the two side by side
measure: The averaged validation on streams every 750 updates, and the first 2,000,000 validation bytes as 16 unbroken streams at the end, with the bits of every piece kept and split by what the context offers (near 256, far 8,192).
reading: The word heads' gain holds with data if their lead over fan2-24k on the long streams at 24,000 updates is at least 0.010 and their lead on the trainer's streams at 24,000 updates is at least two thirds of their lead at 6,000 updates in the same runs; it fades if it falls below that. One seed: a screen.
seen_before_recording: The 6,000-update runs of both arms on the laptop; no 24,000-update run of either exists.
correction: The 'why' first said fifteen times; the full size's 368.6M training bytes are 3.75 times the test bed's 98.3M at 24,000 updates. Corrected before any run started.
